newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end off, falling as US stocks drop.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end off, falling as US stocks drop.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed off in thin trade, tracking a fall in U.S. share prices, with local companies with American Depository Receipt (ADR) issues hardest hit, traders said.

"The Venezuelan market, as with all Latin America bolsas, was hurt today by the fall in the New York Stock Exchange on fears of further interest rate rises," said Multinvest broker Jose Gregorio Tineo.
The U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates 0.25 percentage point last week and many investors fear it may give them a second nudge upwards in coming months.
Venezuela's largest listed company, telephone company CANTV, fell 37.00 bolivars to end at 2054.00.
"The market got off to a good start on the prospect of a decision on the CANTV dividend but then softened when the decision was postponed to this afternoon," said Cavelba broker Eduardo Blanco.
CANTV president Gustavo Roosen said Monday the executive board would be meeting to decide on whether to bring forward a dividend payment previously scheduled for 1998.

The bolsa's .IBC index slipped 0.2 percent to close at 6,331.90 points as a scanty five million shares traded, worth 1.4 billion bolivars ($2.9 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.
Merinvest's composite .MRCP index, which includes CANTV, fell 0.84 points to end at 96.76 points. Among traded issues, 15 fell, 10 rose and seven closed flat.
"While investors are worried about New York, we're not going to see any clear trading trend here," said Blanco.
